name: ChatComposer
intent: The box people write to the assistant in: what the question is about, what is attached, the words, and the toolbar that sends it.
usage: Use ChatComposer at the foot of an assistant panel or a full-screen chat. It is one component: the ask field grows to six lines and then scrolls, Enter sends and Shift plus Enter starts a new line. scopeLabel adds the Scope to this page checkbox on top, naming the page the person is on; onScopeClose puts a close button at the end of that row so the whole row can be shut. attachments shows the files and fields going with the message, each a kit Badge you can take off, and the bar is gone when there are none. The toolbar holds add (a kit DropdownMenu when you pass addMenu), select fields, dictate, Deep Thought and send; send is off until something is typed. Select fields and dictate are switches: while one is on it turns red and says how to stop. See contracts/chatcomposer.json for the full contract.

value.note: Controlled text. Leave it out to let the box keep its own.

onSend.note: The message was sent, by the button or by Enter. The box clears itself.

placeholder.note: The grey line in an empty box.

hints.note: Lines that turn over while the box is empty, like Ask questions, Analyze data, Build dashboards. They stand still when the person prefers reduced motion.

scopeLabel.note: What the question can be scoped to, like Accounts page. Pass it only on a screen there is something to scope to; without it there is no scope row.

onScopeClose.note: The close button at the end of the scope row was pressed. Without it there is no close button; with it, the screen stops passing scopeLabel.

attachments.note: Files and fields going with the message, like Raw-Data.xls or Account Name.

onAttachmentRemove.note: The × on a chip was pressed.

addMenu.note: What the add button offers, like Add file or image and Run playbook. Without it, add is a plain button.

onAdd.note: A pick from the add menu, or add with no menu.

selecting.note: The person is picking fields on the page. The button turns red and says Stop field selection.

dictating.note: The microphone is on. The button turns red and says Stop dictation.

mode.note: quick answers fast; deep thinks longer. The button stays lit on deep. It only shows when onModeChange is set.

disabled.note: Nothing can be typed or pressed, like while the assistant is answering.

label.note: Names the field for screen readers.

useWhen: The foot of an assistant panel or a full-screen chat.
A question that can be scoped to a page, or carry files and fields.
doNot: Do not build the box from Textarea and Buttons, or add a MessageBox, PromptInput or SendButton. Use this.
Do not use it for an ordinary form field. Use Textarea.
Do not show the scope row on a screen with nothing to scope to, and do not name a page the person is not on.
Do not leave the attachment bar showing when nothing is attached.
Do not add a second primary Button beside send.
a11y: The ask field has a hidden label, so it is announced even though the box shows none.
Enter sends and Shift plus Enter starts a new line.
Every toolbar button says what it does, with a kit Tooltip on hover and focus, and says how to stop while it is on.
Send is disabled until something is typed.
The hint lines stand still when the person prefers reduced motion.
